EO 11758 (signed 1974-01-15; 39 FR 2075; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11758.txt, read in full) delegates presidential authority under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 to the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the Secretary of Labor, authorizes agency heads to exempt contracts from section 503, and requires procurement regulations to carry a section 503 compliance provision. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11758 delegating authority of the President under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 at 39 FR 2075, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory held section 1 and one run covering sections 2, 3 and 4, so I replaced it with four clauses (inventory override): sections 1, 2, 3 and 4. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; sections 1 and 4 were amended by later orders held as actor texts (EO 11784, EO 11867 and EO 12608), recorded as later events, and none of them revokes the order or any section. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11758 finds EO 11784 (amends section 1), EO 11867 (revises section 1), EO 12608 (amends section 4), the order's own Federal Register copy, the 1989 codification snapshot and Federal Register rules that cite it as authority; EO 11784 and EO 11867 are the amendments of section 1 and EO 12608 the amendment of section 4, each attached to its clause as a later event with its effective date. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 9, 9 and 6 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text, the held later amendments and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the text of 29 U.S.C. 790 and of section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act as now codified is not held, and the held rules citing the order are leads that its sections 2 to 4 continue, not quoted because they are not packet sources.
savings_reason: EO 11758 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause, and its amendments strike or restate text without ending any clause, so no residual effect is claimed apart from the continuing amended clauses.
earlier_end_check: No section has an own-terms end. EO 11784 and EO 11867 amend section 1 and EO 12608 amends section 4; none revokes or supersedes the order or a section, and no other held order text, statute text or search result does.
scope_check: The corrected inventory has four clauses covering the whole order: sections 1, 2, 3 and 4.
independent_command_check: Section 1 (Director of OMB), section 2 (Secretary of Labor regulations and guidelines), section 3 (agency exemption authority) and section 4 (procurement regulation clause) are separate; section 1's section 5 limb left the clause by amendment to another officer, while its section 500(a) limb and sections 2 to 4 continue.
savings_check: The order has no savings or transition clause; the amendments are strike-and-insert or restatements, so no savings source other than the order itself is needed.

EO 11494 (signed 1969-11-13; 34 FR 18291; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11494.txt, read in full) establishes the Presidential Citizens Medal. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11494 establishing the Presidential Citizens Medal at 34 FR 18291, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory held subsection (b) and a run of subsection (c) with sections 3 and 4 only, so I replaced it with six clauses (inventory override): sections 1, 2(a), 2(b), 2(c), 3 and 4. Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; the only own-text signal for the word terminate is section 4's statement that the Medal does not terminate any other medal, which ends nothing in this order. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11494 finds only the order's own Federal Register copy and the 1989 codification snapshot; the dossier chain has no event and its missing list has only the two standing current-law lines, which I read and rule out as bases because the basis of this claim is the held original text. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 0 hits for the order. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); section 3's design duty is carried as continuing because no held source shows its performance.
savings_reason: EO 11494 has no savings, transition or accrued-rights clause (section 4 only preserves other medals and orders), and no held instrument ends any section, so no residual effect beyond the continuing sections is claimed.
earlier_end_check: No section has an own-terms end. Section 4 says the order does not terminate any other medal or supersede any other order, which is not an end of this order. No held order text, statute text or search result revokes, supersedes or amends EO 11494.
scope_check: The corrected inventory has six clauses covering the whole order: sections 1, 2(a), 2(b), 2(c), 3 and 4.
independent_command_check: Section 1's establishment, section 2's discretionary award rules, section 3's design duty and section 4's rule of construction are separate; none was found ended, and section 3 is not treated as exhausted because no held source shows the design was prepared.
savings_check: The order has no savings or transition clause; section 4's preservation of other medals and orders is a rule of construction, and no ended clause exists to need a savings source.
